reason: The paragraph sign, which this print sets as a swash italic P and the house rule (conventions §2) transcribes P, as in note e of the same annotation (l. iij. P. falsus); unconfirmed by the transcribers either way, and the translation (§ Sed et si quidem) is the same.
qui fi. sint leg. = the Decretals title Qui filii sint legitimi (X 4.17), cited in full in note b (qui fil. sint leg.); 'qui si' is no title.
P. final. = § final, the last paragraph of c. Cum inhibitio; 'P. si nal.' is nothing.
A point after the abbreviation c. (capitulum), present or absent; both readings give the same citation (c. In nostra, de testibus) and only the page image can decide.

The marker alphabet runs a2, b2 and then c; the margin of p072 carries an orphan note keyed c (Aud. itaque. C. con. de suc.) that serves this marker, and the p073 note keyed c belongs by content (hearsay) to annot-053's {c}; the print's c and e are near twins.

The print has a plain c and the note that serves it is the p073 note keyed c (c. tam literis… de testib.), now listed under annot-052; there is no second c on the page once that note is placed here, so the suffix of c2 has nothing to mark.

Kept as e2 to match the key of the margin note that serves it; both readings translate the same. The suffix exists only because annot-052's third marker was read as e on this page, and once that marker is corrected to c (p073-b0l1-1) both this marker and the note's key should drop the suffix and read e.
The alphabet runs h then i and the margin note is keyed i; l would skip i and k, and the italic i and l of the print are near twins.
An accent present or absent on preallegué ('cited before'); the margin has allegué (note d) and allegue (note e2) both, and the readings translate the same.
